title: Sugarcane farmers block highways across Karnataka for higher prices

tea.why: Sugarcane farmers are protesting to demand higher prices for their produce and the implementation of the Swaminathan Commission's report.
tea.want: Farmers demand a minimum support price of at least 5,500 rupees per tonne of sugarcane and 60 rupees per kg of sugar.
tea.changed: Oct 15: Farmers welcomed a newly formed central committee led by Ramesh Chand but stated they will continue their agitation.

summary: Sugarcane growers blocked national highways and key roads at several locations across Karnataka, including Belagavi, Bagalkot, Vijayapura, Kalaburagi, and Dharwad districts, causing traffic disruptions. The demonstrations were organized by farmer groups, including Hasiru Sene and Maharashtra Shetkari Sanghatan. Protesters lay down in front of vehicles and demanded a higher minimum support price, a revised fair and remunerative price, and the implementation of recommendations from the Swaminathan Commission. Although the Union Government formed a four-member committee headed by agriculture scientist Ramesh Chand to examine their demands, farmer leaders announced they would maintain their protest until revised prices are officially announced. Union Food Minister Pralhad Joshi appealed to farmers to withdraw the agitation, assuring them that the Centre would address their concerns, while state cooperation minister Laxman Savadi expressed disappointment regarding the Union Government's handling of the issue.
demands: Increase the Minimum Support Price for sugar to at least 60 rupees per kg
Set the Fair and Remunerative Price for sugarcane to at least 5,500 rupees per tonne
Implement the recommendations of the Swaminathan Commission
response: Union Food Minister Pralhad Joshi appealed to farmers to withdraw their agitation and assured that the Centre would address their concerns, while Karnataka Minister for Cooperation Laxman Savadi criticized the Union Government's approach.

updates.text: Sugarcane farmers blocked national highways at several places in Karnataka, disrupting traffic.
Sugarcane growers blocked roads in Kalaburagi demanding a minimum price of 5,500 rupees per tonne.
Farmers welcomed a federal committee on price issues but stated they would continue their protests until demands are met.
